evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is self-contained and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators via a game URL inherently requires a game to exist (creation of the game).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round is an action that inherently occurs within a game, so it depends on game creation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Showing the session's items requires those items to exist (e.g., added or entered in rounds), so it depends on item-creation stories.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item presupposes that items exist (added/entered elsewhere), so it depends on item-creation/entry stories.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items is an in-game action and therefore inherently depends on having a game (created beforehand).

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires the existence of items (added or entered previously), so it depends on item creation stories.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item presupposes that items exist in a game, so it depends on item-creation/entry and game creation stories.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates requires that estimators have submitted estimates and participants have joined, so it depends on estimator participation/submit features.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates exist from participants, so it depends on estimator submission/join functionality.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling an estimate presumes that estimators can show cards (submit estimates) and that multiple estimators exist in the game.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate follows a round and requires the round/game context, so it depends on round-starting/game creation.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating an earlier story requires storage of previous stories/estimates (history/transcript), so it depends on prior-round storage/viewing stories.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories targets a game's list of items, so it inherently depends on having a game to import into.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Pasting stories presupposes a destination (the game's item list), so it depends on game creation.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is a standalone UI/feature that can be implemented without requiring another specific backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript requires that game data and transcripts exist (game creation and storage), so it depends on game creation/storage.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the transcript being available (viewing/storing transcripts), so it depends on the transcript feature.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires that transcripts are produced/stored (transcript viewing/export capability depends on that).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presupposes that games can be created and stored, so it depends on game creation/storage.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is self-contained and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently requires accounts to exist, so it depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presupposes that an account exists, so it depends on account creation/login.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires that accounts exist, so it depends on account creation.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying times in local timezone is a standalone presentation requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders require stored account/email information, so this depends on account creation/storage.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an estimation scale is a self-contained configuration feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A limit on invites presupposes an invitation mechanism to invite estimators, so it depends on the invite feature.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a URL presupposes that a game and invite/URL mechanism exist, so it depends on game creation and invitation features.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires a round to be started/ item to be present, so it depends on the round/item creation story.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the session's items requires those items to be present (added/imported/entered), so it depends on item-creation/listing stories.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This is a UI/notification feature about estimate submissions and can be implemented as a standalone feature without requiring a different backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates once everyone has submitted depends on knowing who has joined (participant list), so it depends on the join/participant feature.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: The ability to change until the last selection requires knowledge of participants and their submissions, so it depends on join/submission features.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Displaying prior estimates requires storage and retrieval of past estimates (history), so it depends on prior-round storage/scrolling/transcript features.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing per-estimator estimates requires submissions and knowledge of who joined, so it depends on join and estimate submission features.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer is a standalone feature that does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset on 'all play an estimate' requires detection of all participants' submissions (participant/join and submit features), so it depends on join/submission stories.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back through prior rounds requires that prior rounds and their data are stored, so it depends on round creation/storage/transcript features.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining card order is a UI consistency requirement and can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing until draw completion requires knowledge of draw state and participant submissions, so it depends on join/submission/draw-state features.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a UI feature and need not inherently depend on another specific backlog story (could be implemented independently or with account data).

evaluations.evidence: written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a developer-level non-dependent requirement and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is a standalone documentation feature and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is an implementation task that does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is an independent non-functional requirement and not inherently dependent on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a standalone quality requirement and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is an independent non-functional requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a standalone technical requirement and does not inherently require another story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a self-contained UX requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is an independent UX requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: This is a data-storage/privacy requirement and is a property of storage implementation rather than depending on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics collection/ reporting is a standalone feature request and does not inherently require another specific story to exist first.
